slides.headline: 5 Signs Your Dog Needs a Vet Today
Refusing Food for 24+ Hours
slides.body: If your dog skips more than two consecutive meals, it could indicate pain, nausea, or an underlying condition that needs professional evaluation. [SOURCE NEEDED]

slides.headline: Sudden Lethargy or Weakness
slides.body: A normally active dog becoming unusually tired, reluctant to move, or struggling to stand may be experiencing a serious health issue. Seek veterinary attention promptly. [SOURCE NEEDED]

slides.headline: Difficulty Breathing
slides.body: Rapid, laboured, or noisy breathing, persistent coughing, or blue-tinged gums are emergency signs. Do not wait — visit a vet or call an animal ambulance immediately. [SOURCE NEEDED]

slides.headline: Repeated Vomiting or Diarrhoea
slides.body: Occasional stomach upset may pass, but repeated episodes (more than 2–3 times in a day), especially with blood, require veterinary assessment to rule out infection, toxicity, or obstruction. [SOURCE NEEDED]

slides.headline: Swelling, Limping, or Visible Pain
slides.body: Unexplained swelling, guarding a body part, yelping when touched, or sudden limping can indicate fractures, joint issues, infections, or insect stings that need diagnosis. [SOURCE NEEDED]
